comment: Chunk 2: Mapped model species to likely gene symbols using standard human gene names and common synonyms. For entities representing multi-protein complexes (SMAD2/3/4, ILK_Rictor, CTNNB1–TCF7L2, CTNNB1–HIF1A) I listed each gene as a separate component. For phenotype/structural nodes (Stress_Fibers, Fast_Migration, ApicalBasal_Pol, Horizontal_Pol, Self_Loop, TGFb_ext) I provided the most plausible associated gene(s) (e.g. actin/myosin for stress fibers, MMPs for migration, PAR complex members for apical–basal polarity, VANGL/PRICKLE for planar polarity, TGFB1 for autocrine TGF-β). Where microRNAs appear I used MIR gene symbols (e.g. MIR29C, MIR200C, MIR34A). Names are ranked by likelihood/typical usage.

Chunk 3: Mappings use standard human gene symbols (HGNC/NCBI conventions) inferred from display names. Known multi-protein assemblies (PHD1_2, ORC, Pre_RC, pAPC) are represented as complexes with representative core subunit genes. Non-gene model states/processes (Hypoxia, ROS, Replication, kinetochores states, 4N DNA, Cytokinesis) are left as named entities (treated as 'gene' entries here to satisfy the schema) using commonly used labels.

comment: Chunk 1: I mapped each model species (display name) to the most likely human gene symbols or common synonyms for NCBI Gene lookup. For canonical protein complexes (mTORC1, mTORC2, FocalAdhesions) I returned a complex entry listing typical component genes. For environmental/phenotype nodes (CellDensity, Stiff_ECM, GF, PIP3, DAG, Ca2+, IP3, etc.) I provided the most plausible sensor, enzyme, or proximal gene proxy (e.g., NF2/Merlin or YAP1 for density/mechanical sensing; PIK3CA/PIK3CB as sources/proxies for PIP3) because these model nodes represent non-gene molecular states. Where multiple family members could apply (RAS, RAF, MEK, ERK, PI3K, AKT, GSK3, S6K, 4EBP1), I listed the most likely isoforms first followed by close paralogs; up to three names were given per entity as requested.
